alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad option covers media forms, histories, audiences, representation and production. A second option adds audience markets and organisational strategy. A third emphasises digital culture and computation. All three contain sustained media study and are distinct. Journalism and political communication remain evidenced directions beyond the three-option limit.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: UCR introduces qualitative study of social meaning. Groningen teaches methods for studying media.
Both examine how narratives shape identity. UCR focuses on life and travel writing. Groningen draws on a wider range of media.
Both analyse media forms and representation. Groningen also introduces media production and audiences as research areas.
Both use historical perspectives to understand media. UCR examines the material forms and uses of older media technologies.
Groningen offers a dedicated course on media in everyday life.
Groningen focuses on media audiences and uses. UCR develops related perspectives in psychology and communication.
Both consider changes associated with digital technologies. UCR focuses on business strategy and organisational transformation.
UCR examines how storytelling and power work across television and digital media. Groningen focuses on media networks and platforms.
Both examine media representation. UCR focuses on race, storytelling and power. Groningen also studies archives.
The Documentary brings media analysis and production together in one form. Groningen also considers use across a wider range of media.
Groningen teaches theories of media and power in a separate course.
The example uses the Global Change faculty-wide course.
Groningen requires a dedicated media research seminar after the earlier media theory and analysis courses.
Students select one of the available thematic courses.
Groningen studies specialist media thinkers and theories.
Groningen requires a separate advanced course in media research methods.
Groningen teaches professional writing for different media.
Groningen has a course on career prospects in the media sector.
Groningen has a dedicated course on designing digital futures.
Groningen requires a 30 EC minor.
This example uses Content Creation. At UCR, The Documentary develops production skills, and Creative Communication Laboratory focuses on experimental literary forms.
Groningen requires a media studies thesis. Independent research at UCR is optional.

notes.text: Groningen requires a sequence in media theory, research, platforms and production, plus a thesis. UCR offers related study across media, social science, business and computing. Specialist media research and professional writing have more limited coverage.
This comparison uses the redesigned curriculum for students starting in September 2026.

audience.programmeDescription: Media Studies at the University of Groningen examines media forms, production, audiences and their role in society. Students develop research skills, take a minor and write a thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines media history, representation and production. The other options give greater weight to media industries and audiences or to digital media and computing. Groningen has more dedicated media research and professional courses.
